newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Govt demands action on Sappi pollution.
newsitem.headline: Govt demands action on Sappi pollution.

text.p: Forestry and Water Affairs Minister Kader Asmal has given Sappi Ltd's Saiccor mill six months to come up with a long-term plan to eradicate pollution on Natal's beaches by its Umkomaas mill.

After a meeting with top management on Monday, Asmal told reporters that the company had agreed to build a ligno-sulphate plant costing between 300 million and 500 million rand to reduce ligno-sulphate emissions by between 35 and 40 percent.

The emissions cause the discolouration of water and a thick foam on the beaches 20 km on either side of the mill, which is at the mouth of the Umkomaas River. Local communities have been campaigning for several years to stop the pollution.

Asmal said that another meeting would be held with Sappi on November 19 to consider a report by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research. Asmal said he was "considering extending their permit, which expires on November 3, until June 21 because by that time there should be other options available."

Other options in reducing pollution included extending the pipeline out to sea to 7.5 km from the present three km. Permits are usually issued for periods of five years or more and Asmal said the fact that he was considering only granting a six month permit indicated that he was serious about getting rid of the pollution by the year 2000.
